prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks
For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I have moved my second part from B041 to B023. Base editing (B060) remains my lead: a defined nucleobase deamination was made site-specific, evolved to act on DNA (TadA was an RNA enzyme) and kept free of double-strand breaks, and it has been reproduced in many laboratories and is already used in patients. It is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize because the novelty is a chemical conversion of a base, not a cut. Liu alone is the decisive originator in every statement that discusses attribution. Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling (B023) is the best-reproduced and best-attributed achievement on the list: a ligand-controlled general method used daily for 25 years, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the clear independent pair. The pairing is a molecule-making method plus a chemical tool that reprograms biology. It uses three names and is the second-part pairing that most colleagues have already said they could accept (Somfai proposes it, Aili and Brzezinski call B023 acceptable, Aqvist leads with it).
statement.case_against: Base editing is young, its long-term safety record is short, and it follows the 2020 prize closely. B023 overlaps with the recognised 2010 cross-coupling tradition and leaves Kosugi's 1983 priority question to be settled in the written record. The pairing is a pragmatic coalition rather than one theme, and a Liu-alone credit leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida. I also give up B041, where a new chemical modality is still, in my view, the fresher principle, but where the PROTAC and cereblon glue strands cannot be fitted into three names and no degrader is approved.

responses.point: Pairing B023 with Liu's base editing gives one traditional molecule-making achievement and one chemical-biology achievement within three names, and B041 is a fallback only once approvals or a clearer allocation exist.
responses.response: I now agree with your allocation argument and have moved to your pairing. My earlier B041 part forced Crews and Deshaies alone, which leaves a visible credit gap (Ciulli, Handa), and your point that no approved degrader exists weighs more for me after round 1 than before. I also accept your answer on chemical novelty for B023: C-N bond formation with amines needed its own ligand generations and is not a repeat of the C-C couplings of 2010. I still think Kosugi's tin-amide work should be dismissed in the record rather than only in discussion, but I agree with you that it was not a general catalytic method.

responses.point: B023 combines consequence, maturity and clean credit, with Kosugi as a real precursor, and B041 is still partly forward looking because no approvals are in hand.
responses.response: Your maturity argument against B041 persuaded me. A method confirmed independently for decades is the kind of result I trust most, and I said as much in round 1 when I named B023 my first alternative. I do not agree that B023 should stand alone, because a single mature part would leave out the newest chemistry that changes what can be done to DNA. On Liu alone, I take your trainee and Target-AID worry as real, but the Committee's usual practice and the three-name ceiling favour the principal investigator, and the reports can settle Kondo and Nishida in the record.

responses.point: Degraders open a new therapeutic modality and are fresher in principle than base editing, but Aili would be comfortable with B023 as a second part of a two-part prize.
responses.response: Your objection that base editing is a downstream extension of Cas9 is the strongest one against my lead, and I answer it only partly: the deaminase chemistry and the TadA evolution are separable from the cut. I still think B041 is the fresher principle, which is why I keep it as my first alternative. But your own concession that B023 works as a second part, together with your count that Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli cannot cover the glue strand, makes the B060 plus B023 pairing the one I think can reach five. If a majority prefers B041 after the discussion of cereblon, I would revisit it.

responses.point: Linke asks whether modified-base detection is robust enough to count as a chemical advance and whether Akeson or Branton belongs in a nanopore trio.
responses.response: Direct detection of modified bases by current signal is real and reproduced, and as a nucleotide biochemist I value it, but it is calibrated against LC-MS and antibody-free mapping rather than established as a quantitative chemical readout on its own. That is one reason I keep B039 as an alternative and not a part. On names, I agree with you that Akeson's enzyme ratchet made base reading practical and should come before Branton in a trio, which is a change from my round-1 trio of Bayley, Branton and Deamer. The 1996 Kasianowicz and Branton result remains the founding experiment, so I still cannot see a three-person cut that will not be contested.

responses.point: Brzezinski pairs B060 with a mature mechanistic part (B030) rather than letting base editing carry the prize alone, and calls B023 the better supported choice.
responses.response: We agree that B060 should not stand alone, and that Liu alone is the clean credit. Where we differ is the partner. B030 is a sound and textbook result, but no other member ranked it in the opening, it adds little beyond Marcus theory for a committee seeking a new capability, and your own statement says you would not oppose B023 as the better-supported part. I take that as an opening for a pairing that you and Somfai can both accept.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee will accept a second genome-editing prize so soon after 2020, and whether Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida must be reconsidered.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize makes B023 too incremental, and how the Kosugi 1983 question should be dealt with in the written justification.
Whether a majority of five will accept a two-part prize built from a classical method and a chemical-biology tool rather than a single theme.
Whether B041 should be revisited if the cereblon and PROTAC strands can be given one coherent three-name citation or if a degrader is approved.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent. My work on dNTP pools and replication fidelity is thematically adjacent to nucleic-acid editing and nanopore nucleotide detection, but I have no known collaboration with Liu, Buchwald, Hartwig or any other credited candidate. I have no tie to the pairing I now prefer beyond field proximity.
